title: Use Case Diagram
note: Student actions use browser sessions; no student signup exists. Admin management requires staff authentication and appropriate permissions. Career content and assessment remain demonstrations.

title: System Architecture Diagram
note: The frontend and API share the Django origin in the built application. Vite is a development/build tool, not a required production API server.

title: DFD Level 0
note: A single process shows system inputs and outputs. Student, administrator and maintainer are external actors. Internal tables and processes are intentionally hidden at this level.

title: DFD Level 1
note: D1-D4 are logical stores implemented in one SQLite database. Paired arrows represent request/write data and returned/read data. Community and catalogue results merge with D3 preferences; administration uses Django auth/session tables. Seed import reads bundled JSON.

title: DFD Level 2
note: Decomposition of the create-discussion part of process 2.0. CSRF/method checks precede the view; title/body/tags are validated. The atomic action writes the thread and visitor vote state, then returns refreshed state.

title: Entity Relationship Diagram
note: Only Discussion-to-Answer is an application-model foreign key. Saved college/thread identifiers inside VisitorState JSON are not enforced relational links. No College-to-Discussion or User-to-VisitorState foreign key exists.

title: Flowchart
note: High-level page load and persisted-action flow. Failed POST requests display an error without claiming a successful save. Browser-only tools such as comparison do not require a write request.

title: Activity Diagram
note: Swimlanes assign responsibilities. The happy path validates and saves a new community discussion. The invalid path returns an error and allows correction; no signup is required in the current prototype.

title: Sequence Diagram
note: The save-college sequence represents successful interaction order. Responses use dashed arrows. Refresh persistence follows from another bootstrap GET reading the same browser session. Error sequences are summarized in the API/authentication diagrams.

title: Class Diagram
note: The diagram mirrors the actual Django model classes. Only College and Discussion define __str__. save/delete/query APIs are inherited, not custom methods. There are no fabricated student login or recommendation classes.

title: Component Diagram
note: Component responsibilities are dependencies, not separate deployed services. React has no direct database access. The seed command and admin also use Django models. Framework middleware participates in the request lifecycle.

title: Deployment Diagram
note: Actual deployment is local, not cloud hosting. .venv is outside Campus. A production deployment would need an appropriate WSGI/ASGI server, HTTPS and separate static-file serving; these are future configuration, not currently implemented nodes.

title: Database Schema Diagram
note: All application fields are included. Session key fields are not database foreign keys. Django additionally manages auth, session, permission, content-type, migration and admin-log tables; those framework tables are listed in the accompanying README.

title: Wireframe Diagram
note: Low-fidelity structural wireframes of three existing screens. This is not a pixel-exact screenshot. Shared header and mobile bottom navigation remain outside screen content; dialogs/drawers appear as overlays.

title: Sitemap
note: Logical screen hierarchy for the SPA. Dashboard, careers, colleges and community are React views under /. Admin is a distinct Django route. The overlays are application dialogs, not additional website pages.

title: User Flow Diagram
note: Shows three real navigation journeys. Only actions wired to the API persist. Comparison selection and roadmap task state remain temporary UI state; mentor questions are stored without external delivery.

title: State Diagram
note: State machine for one college bookmark, not a whole student profile. Initial state comes from session-aware bootstrap. A successful POST toggles the stored flag. An unsuccessful request leaves the last confirmed state unchanged.

title: API Flow Diagram
note: api.ts handles bootstrap and action calls; DiscussionDetailScreen fetches the thread-answer endpoint directly. Normal responses contain refreshed state or answer data. Error responses must not be interpreted as successful database saves.

title: Authentication Flow Diagram
note: This is Django admin session authentication, not JWT or student authentication. Django checks active/staff status and model permissions; a superuser has broad permissions. Student API actions currently use visitor sessions, not registered student ownership.

title: Network Architecture Diagram
note: The implemented environment uses local HTTP on loopback. External font/image requests need internet. This is not a deployed internet service; HTTPS termination, firewall policy and production hosting are future infrastructure. No JWT or cloud database is present.

title: Gantt Chart
note: No development schedule was provided. This chart is an explicitly proposed six-week improvement plan, with relative weeks rather than invented completion dates. Scope and timing are subject to mentor review.

title: Context Diagram
note: Context and DFD Level 0 intentionally cover the same system boundary. This view emphasizes external actors, while the DFD labels the single process as 0. No mentor-delivery platform, payment service or AI API is connected.
